**5B.9 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin (2024)**

**Verdict:** mixed, leaning negative. Thailand avoided a major macro collapse and tourism helped the recovery, but Srettha repeatedly pushed a large, fiscally controversial handout and publicly pressed the central bank for rate cuts. On crisis management, his Myanmar-border posture looked more competent and restrained than his macro-fiscal posture.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Monetary Policy Committee’s Decision 3/2024** | Bank of Thailand | June 12, 2024 | [URL](https://www.bot.or.th/en/news-and-media/news/news-20240612.html)  
  The BOT said the economy was expanding mainly through domestic demand and tourism, inflation was still low, and the policy rate was held to preserve macro-financial stability. This supports a partial positive reading on competence in managing inflation and recovery, though it is BOT’s assessment rather than Srettha’s direct authorship.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`

- **Thailand Economic Monitor July 2024: Unlocking the Growth Potential of Secondary Cities** | World Bank | July 2024 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/thailand/publication/temjuly2024)  
  The World Bank projected 2.4% growth, but warned that public debt and the fiscal deficit would rise as stimulus was implemented and urged more targeted transfers. This is mixed evidence: growth held up, but the policy mix looked fiscally stretched.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.1`

- **Thailand’s cabinet approves $13.5 billion digital-wallet handout** | Reuters via Investing.com | April 23, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007)  
  Reuters reported a 10,000-baht transfer to 50 million Thais and noted immediate debt and fiscal-risk criticism. This is strong negative evidence for competence and honesty because the flagship response was broad, politically salient, and fiscally controversial from the start.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`, `5B.7`

- **Thai PM says digital-wallet scheme will spur jobs and manufacturing** | Reuters via Investing.com | July 11, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-digital-wallet-scheme-will-spur-jobs-and-manufacturing-3514879)  
  Srettha defended the handout as a jobs-and-manufacturing stimulus. That is weak positive evidence for a stated policy rationale, but it also shows continued reliance on a slogan-friendly flagship rather than a clearly evidence-corrective response.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.7`, `5B.1`, `5B.6`

- **Thailand’s flagship $14 billion handout hits implementation snags** | Reuters via Yahoo News | August 1, 2024 | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html)  
  Reuters reported launch snags and criticism from economists and former central bankers who called the scheme fiscally risky. That strengthens the negative side: the government stayed the course despite expert objections and implementation friction.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.7`, `5B.1`

- **Thai PM: central bank should cut rates by at least 25 bps** | Reuters via ThePrint | April 8, 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/thai-pm-central-bank-should-cut-rates-by-at-least-25-bps/2032207/)  
  Srettha publicly urged the central bank to cut rates while the government pushed the digital-wallet plan. This is negative evidence for competence and honesty in macro management because it shows political pressure on an independent technocratic institution.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.2`, `5B.7`

- **Daughter of Thai heavyweight Thaksin calls central bank independence an obstacle** | Reuters via ThePrint | May 3, 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/daughter-of-thai-heavyweight-thaksin-calls-central-bank-independence-an-obstacle/2068726/)  
  Reuters said Srettha repeatedly pushed rate cuts and that his political camp treated BOT independence as an obstacle. This is strong negative evidence for evidence-based macro management and respect for institutional expertise.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.2`, `5B.7`

- **Press Release on the Economic and Monetary Conditions for June and the Second Quarter of 2024** | Bank of Thailand | July 31, 2024 | [URL](https://www.bot.or.th/en/news-and-media/news/news-20240731.html)  
  The BOT described growth as uneven but still expanding, with inflation driven partly by energy and food and labor market conditions improving steadily. The same release noted that government spending had expanded significantly after the budget was enacted. This supports a mixed but not catastrophic management record.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`

- **Thailand working ‘relentlessly’ to solve Myanmar crisis - Srettha** | Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News | May 24, 2024 | [URL](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha)  
  Srettha said Thailand was working to end the Myanmar crisis and reduce spillover violence. That is positive evidence for crisis management competence, especially because the posture emphasized containment rather than escalation.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `5B.7`

- **Thai Youth Activist Dies in Custody** | Human Rights Watch | May 14, 2024 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/14/thai-youth-activist-dies-custody)  
  HRW said Srettha vowed strict enforcement of lèse-majesté and that repressive prosecutions remained the norm. While not economic policy, it undercuts the claim that the government was generally honest about rights-risk tradeoffs and capacity to reform inherited problems.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.7`, `5B.8`

**5B.9 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin (2024)**

**Verdict:** mixed, leaning negative. Thailand did not face a sanctions episode, and the broad macro picture was not catastrophic, but Srettha’s flagship response was a fiscally risky cash-transfer plan that drew sustained expert criticism. The strongest positive evidence is on crisis containment around Myanmar and some later policy adjustment.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Monetary Policy Committee’s Decision 3/2024** | Bank of Thailand | June 12, 2024 | [URL](https://www.bot.or.th/en/news-and-media/news/news-20240612.html)  
  The BOT described 2024 as a slow, structurally constrained recovery driven by domestic demand, tourism, and government disbursement. That supports a partial competence reading, though it is the central bank’s assessment rather than Srettha’s own.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`

- **Thailand Economic Monitor July 2024: Unlocking the Growth Potential of Secondary Cities** | World Bank | July 2024 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/thailand/publication/temjuly2024)  
  The World Bank projected 2.4% growth but warned that public debt and the fiscal deficit would rise as stimulus measures were implemented, and it urged more targeted support. This is mixed evidence: not a collapse, but a clearly stressed fiscal position.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.1`

- **Thailand’s cabinet approves $13.5 billion digital-wallet handout** | Reuters via Investing.com | April 23, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thailands-cabinet-approves-135-billion-digital-wallet-handout-3390007)  
  Reuters said the plan was a 10,000-baht transfer to 50 million Thais and noted debt and fiscal-risk criticism from the outset. This is strong negative evidence for competence and honesty in macro management because the policy was broad, visible, and controversial immediately.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`, `5B.7`

- **Thai PM says digital-wallet scheme will spur jobs and manufacturing** | Reuters via Investing.com | July 11, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-digital-wallet-scheme-will-spur-jobs-and-manufacturing-3514879)  
  Srettha defended the handout as a jobs-and-manufacturing stimulus. That is weak positive evidence for a stated growth rationale, but it also shows continued reliance on a slogan-friendly flagship rather than a clearly corrective policy pivot.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.7`, `5B.1`, `5B.6`

- **Thailand’s flagship $14 billion handout hits implementation snags** | Reuters via Yahoo News | August 1, 2024 | [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/thailands-flagship-14-billion-handout-072635149.html)  
  Reuters reported launch snags and criticism from economists and former central bankers who called the scheme fiscally risky. This strengthens the negative case: the government kept pushing a disputed plan despite expert warnings.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.7`, `5B.1`

- **Thai central bank holds key rate, defies government calls for cuts** | Reuters via Investing.com | April 10, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-central-bank-holds-key-rate-defies-government-calls-for-cuts-3372713)  
  Reuters reported that the Bank of Thailand resisted repeated government calls to cut rates. That is negative evidence for competence and honesty because the government was publicly pressuring an independent technocratic institution for short-term relief.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.2`, `5B.7`

- **Daughter of Thai heavyweight Thaksin calls central bank independence an obstacle** | Reuters via ThePrint | May 3, 2024 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/daughter-of-thai-heavyweight-thaksin-calls-central-bank-independence-an-obstacle/2068726/)  
  Reuters said Srettha repeatedly pushed rate cuts and that his political camp treated BOT independence as an obstacle. This is strong negative evidence that macro policy was being driven by political pressure rather than disciplined correction.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.3`, `5B.2`, `5B.7`

- **Thailand working ‘relentlessly’ to solve Myanmar crisis - Srettha** | Bangkok Post, reporting Bloomberg News | May 24, 2024 | [URL](https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2798697/thailand-working-relentlessly-to-solve-myanmar-crisis-srettha)  
  Srettha said Thailand was working to reduce spillover violence and end the Myanmar crisis. That is the clearest positive evidence for crisis management competence and a restrained public line.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `5B.7`

- **Thai PM says part of $13 billion digital wallet stimulus to be in cash** | Reuters via Investing.com | September 3, 2024 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-pm-says-part-of-13-billion-digital-wallet-stimulus-to-be-in-cash-3597164)  
  The government shifted part of the digital-wallet plan into cash payments. This is the best available correction evidence, but it looks more like tactical compromise than a clean admission that the original design was mistaken.  
  Question IDs: `5B.9`, `5B.1`, `5B.7`

**Search Gap**

- I did not find strong direct evidence on sanctions management, because Thailand was not under a major sanctions shock in 2024.
- I also did not find a clear, documented cycle of “announce policy, measure failure, openly reverse course” beyond the partial shift of the digital-wallet plan into cash.
- So the record is strongest on one negative macro-fiscal pattern and one positive crisis-management pattern, but weaker on explicit, transparent learning from mistakes.
